investigation: Trace current behavior with pstack-how; investigate rationale with pstack-why only if needed.
Check claims and return evidence, inference and unknowns.
bug-fix: Form hypotheses and discriminate using runtime evidence; trace the surviving root cause.
Define the smallest fix and a cheap regression test when available.
Apply the fix, verify the original trigger and nearby behavior, inspect the diff.
perf-issue: Record a representative baseline and conditions.
Repeat equivalent runs and apply pstack-benchmark-checklist before claiming a gain.
hillclimb: Name one metric, target, fixed workload and attempt limit.
Loop hypothesis, experiment and equivalent before/after measurement.
Keep only measured semantic-preserving wins; revert rejected candidates.
Commit accepted units only when committing was authorized.
runtime-forensics: Observe the live symptom in the authorized environment.
Separate correlation from a proved mechanism.
Remove temporary instrumentation and verify any authorized correction.
trace-forensics: Identify the captured artifact, workload and time window.
Read stacks, timing, allocations and sampling limitations.
Correlate with source and available runtime evidence.
Report the mechanism and evidence gaps without pretending the artifact proves an unobserved event.
feature: Define user-visible behavior, data shape and acceptance checks.
Ground existing ownership and sketch boundaries.
Implement the smallest coherent behavior unit.
Verify happy/error paths through the actual interface and assess blast radius.
refactoring: State behavior that must remain unchanged and establish checks.
Remove redundant structure before adding abstraction.
Refactor bounded units and migrate callers.
Verify behavior and delete obsolete internal APIs when safe.
prototype: State the decision the prototype should resolve.
Build bounded competing alternatives sequentially unless parallel workers were requested.
Keep the useful evidence; do not ship throwaway code implicitly.
visual-parity: Capture the actual baseline at named viewport/state.
Compare implementation and reference at the same conditions.
Verify desktop/mobile and relevant interactive states; do not infer parity from source.
authoring-a-skill: Define the real trigger and boundaries.
Write concise SKILL.md metadata and instructions with progressive disclosure.
Keep optional helpers scoped and deterministic.
Validate metadata, references, triggers and permission-sensitive cases.
eval: Define a behavioral claim and representative positive/negative cases.
Use blinded equivalent conditions when independent reviewers are authorized.
Execute only explicitly authorized agent runs; no hidden paid calls.
Separate deterministic checks from model behavioral results and report limitations.
babysit: Inspect the named PR/stack, current head, CI and unresolved review threads.
Fix only confirmed issues within scope; do not dismiss relevant failures as flaky without proof.
Report merge readiness; merge only with explicit authorization.
shipping: Confirm explicit publication/merge authorization and target.
Independently verify the exact artifact and required gates if authorized reviewers are available.
Ship only the contiguous verified units in dependency order.
Verify the remote result; do not infer deployment readiness from push output.
autonomous-run: Confirm the goal, permitted operations, target and attempt/time limits.
Execute bounded verifiable units; do not create recurring automation implicitly.
Stop at missing permission, ambiguous material decisions or unavailable evidence.
Leave a scoped decision trail and current-state handoff.
orchestrate: Define slices, dependencies, write ownership and acceptance checks.
Use sequential execution unless the human explicitly requests subagents.
Use isolated native workers only when available and authorized.
Verify aggregate results and report unresolved dependencies; do not create other chats implicitly.
autopilot-full: Confirm authorization for each external write and merge target.
Own each independent PR from implementation to exact-head verification.
Use authorized native workers or disclosed sequential ownership.
Merge only verified permitted PRs; stop if a gate or permission is missing.
autopilot-stack: Define a linear sequence of independently verifiable changes.
Build and verify each bounded unit against its predecessor.
Publish the stack only when requested.
Leave it reviewable; this playbook is not merge authorization.
session-pickup: Read the specifically requested prior session and scope.
Check live branches, changed files and artifacts against the handoff.
Preserve others' in-flight work and identify stale assumptions.
Resume only the authorized remaining task.
pause-safely: Stop only this task's processes and workers.
Preserve work and record branch, files, evidence and unfinished steps.
Do not kill shared servers or delete worktrees implicitly.
Provide a resumable handoff and respect the requested pause.
multi-phase-plan: Define outcomes and acceptance checks per phase.
Order small units so each leaves a verifiable state.
Identify material dependencies and permission gates.
Execute only the requested phase; planning is not approval for all phases.
worktree-cleanup: Inventory only relevant worktrees and prove ownership/status.
Check uncommitted, untracked, ignored and unpushed data.
Use a recoverable archive or human-confirmed deletion; preserve needed ignored files.
Never clean another chat's worktree or simulator implicitly.
opening-a-pr: Confirm PR publication authorization and applicable issue-first rules.
Inspect the exact diff, branch/base and behavior checks.
Use Conventional Commits without AI attribution and a concise why/scope/risk/verification body.
Create through native tools when available, attach it, and verify its remote head and state. Do not merge implicitly.
